summary: The prewarmer correctly deduplicates queued registrations, keeps startup non-blocking, records timing information, and isolates ordinary per-repository failures. Its main weaknesses are incomplete cancellation propagation, overly broad treatment of OperationCanceledException, an unbounded backlog, and limited observability for callers and tests. The supplied .NET analyzer reported no findings; no coverage evidence was available.

grade.rationale: Normal queue processing and cleanup are correct, but an active synchronous scan cannot observe the stopping token, and an unrelated cancellation exception can end the worker.
The class is small and dependencies are explicit, although queue-key construction is duplicated and backlog policy is implicit.
Naming and control flow clearly express the prewarming workflow, but the cancellation and deduplication semantics are not evident from the public API.
Ordinary repository failures are logged and isolated, but every OperationCanceledException bypasses that handling even when shutdown was not requested.
Core collaborators are injected, but callers receive no completion result and must observe asynchronous processing through polling, cache effects, or logs.

findings.title: Unrelated cancellation exceptions terminate the background worker
findings.description: The catch filter excludes every OperationCanceledException, not only cancellation caused by stoppingToken. If a dependency throws OperationCanceledException for any other reason, it escapes ExecuteAsync and permanently terminates the service; under the default BackgroundService exception behavior this may also stop the host.
findings.recommendation: Handle OperationCanceledException as expected shutdown only when stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested. Log and isolate other cancellation exceptions in the same way as other per-registration failures.

findings.title: Stopping token cannot cancel a scan once it has started
findings.description: Passing stoppingToken to Task.Run only prevents the delegate from starting when cancellation has already occurred; it cannot interrupt GetMeasured after execution begins. A slow or blocked repository scan can therefore continue through shutdown and delay or outlive service termination.
findings.recommendation: Add cancellation support to GetMeasured and pass stoppingToken through the scanning operations. If that API cannot be changed, explicitly document and bound shutdown behavior rather than implying that Task.Run provides cooperative cancellation.

findings.title: Unbounded queue provides no backlog limit or backpressure
findings.description: Every distinct registration configuration can remain in both the channel and pending dictionary while the single consumer performs potentially expensive scans. A sustained producer or unusually large registry can cause unchecked memory growth and an increasingly stale backlog.
findings.recommendation: Use a bounded channel with an explicit full-queue policy, or otherwise impose a maximum backlog and expose/log rejected or coalesced requests.

findings.title: Queue callers cannot observe completion or failure
findings.description: Queue and QueueAll return immediately without a task, result, or idle signal. Callers and tests cannot deterministically know when a requested prewarm has completed or whether it failed, leaving them dependent on polling cache state or intercepting logs.
findings.recommendation: Provide an internal or public awaitable enqueue operation, completion handle, or drain/idle hook while retaining the fire-and-forget methods where appropriate.
